narrative: Demand for PL1__M3FEC07A is continuous and variable (CV=0.331) with a log-normal profile and no detectable trend across the 137-day observation window. Lead times are moderately unstable (CV=0.373) with a mean of 4.08 days after removal of two data-error outliers. The combined lead-time demand sigma of 1,223 units drives a statistically required safety stock of 2,012 units — far above the current SAP value of 182. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with r=5,011 and Q=4,572 (capacity-constrained from an unconstrained EOQ of 12,140) achieves the 95% service level while reducing total annual costs by 41.5%.
warnings: Safety stock increases by 1005.5% from SAP baseline — significant working capital commitment required
Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ of 12,140 reduced to 4,572 units

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (non-zero fraction = 100%), moderately variable (CV=0.331), and non-intermittent — making a continuous-review (r,Q) model the standard economic choice. The policy balances ordering and holding costs via the EOQ formula while the reorder point provides the required service buffer against lead-time demand variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap of 6,584.95 units binds tightly: with safety stock at 2,012 only 4,572 units of order quantity are permitted versus the unconstrained EOQ of 12,140. This increases ordering frequency (58.6 vs theoretical 22 orders/year) and raises ordering costs. If storage capacity can be expanded, significant further savings are achievable.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (2,192) + safety_stock (2,012) = 4,204 < max_storage_units (6,584.95); policy is feasible.
